Current extraction validation

November 1, 2026 · After source-grounded numerical normalization. Earlier dated validation snapshot

R2: 687 source-qualified records, 134 unresolved

All 821 reports have a Sol screening record. Extraction now has 687 source-qualified records: the earlier 598 plus 79 previously validated notation recoveries and 10 newly verified normalized records. Screening and numerical extraction remain separate.

The earlier 223 recorded holds remain in the history; 134 is the current unresolved extraction count. Among the 171 reports whose first recorded error concerned numeric notation, 89 are now qualified and 82 remain unresolved. They were not all assumed to be simple word-number errors.

New normalization coverage holds on 87 previously qualified records do not revoke their earlier source qualification. Source/model conflicts and ambiguous conversions still require review.

R3: 296 source-qualified current fragments across 157 articles

The current numerical pass produced 263 originally source-checked fragments. Another 33 originally held responses now pass the full source and model checks as separately linked normalized views. The current 726 scientific responses therefore include 296 qualified fragments and 430 unresolved fragments; 45 provider-problem tasks have no scientific response. These are fragment and task counts, not completed full-text reviews.

Original response states remain unchanged. The original eight-request pilot remains 3 passed and 5 held under its original rules. Its current follow-up is:

Neither normalization nor fragment validation establishes whole-report completion, clinical validation, pooling eligibility, an inferred sample size, or a default confidence level.

Numbers and source details

Numeric analysis values use Arabic numbers. Missing or nonestimable point values display as NA, with their original reasons retained. Reported zero values, inequalities, units, and explicit confidence levels are preserved. Source-only dates and ranges remain annotations and do not become fitted sample sizes or point estimates. Open an article title to inspect its source passages, model/population scope, original wrappers, and normalized views.
